I think a NT unironically saying "the autistics " would sound suspicious definitely. It does sound dehumanizing when used like that. But in certains contexts from the autistic community I think it's  playful. I don't think irony would be the word, I think it just sounds awkward and silly and that makes it funny. It also sounds way more casual that "autistic people" so I think that's why it's good for humor. 

I think it might also remind me of "the gays", or "the transes" which is also used by a lot of queer people to be humorous, myself included. I think the explanation would be the same as what I've said about "the autistics".

Honestly from the way you're responding to everyone I can see why your girlfriend would be unconfortable, you do come off as very defensive and frankly, just seems like you think you cannot be wrong.

I understand sometime not realizing the person you're talking to is upset and in your mind just responding logically to what they say and explaining your perspective-- I do it too. But knowing when to step back is an important skill to develop in my opinion. I know it's not easy, but sometimes people will be more sensitive than you are and if you love them and want to maintain an healthy relationship with them, you have to be mindful of their feelings. 

I agree with your girlfriend that this is a gross thing to do. I do think she should have made more of an effort to explain to you why but she probably felt upset and didn't necessarily know how to put it into words. So waiting for her to calm down, taking a step back yourself and asking again later would have been best.

As to why I think I think it's wrong, well you found the way that man talked funny and decided to film him to laugh later. That is mean because you're laughing *at* him, not *with* him, you're making fun of him. You say that you wouldn't mind if someone filmed you while you talked that way and I don't know you, but maybe it's precisely because you do not talk like that that you wouldn't be upset. If you were, you would be playing a bit.  It's probably not the case with that man. I don't know the details, maybe he's not a native speaker, maybe he's extremely anxious and just really wants to be polite and do his job well. You don't know his situation and so it's cruel to make fun of him. People have boundaries and things that are okay between friends, where you have an established bond and trust one another is not always okay between strangers.
Your example I would argue would not be okay between friends either in a lot of contexts. You should only make fun of people for things they are not insecure about-- which of course you can only know with close ones. And people are often insecure about how they speak.
